My land is about 10 mu. I have farmed it for over 40 years. My children are in the city now, so it is just me and my wife working the fields. I do not need to think long about what to grow — it is wheat in winter and corn in summer. That is what everyone here does. That is what my father did. The soil and the water here are suited for it, and I know how to do it.

For wheat, I will buy Jimai seeds from the supply shop in town — they are what the neighbors use and the yield is decent. I always apply enough fertilizer to make sure the crop does not go hungry. I put down diammonium phosphate and urea, same as always — I do not measure precisely but roughly what the shop recommends. Wheat needs water badly here in Quzhou, especially before the rains come. I will irrigate four times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading, and once when the grain is filling. That is what it takes. I spray herbicide in the autumn and again if weeds come back, and I watch for rust and aphids in spring.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June. Hybrid seed is just what you buy now — everyone uses it. Summer rains help so I only irrigate once or twice if July is dry. I apply fertilizer at planting and again when the corn is knee-high. I spray for corn borer if I see it.

I do not experiment. I am 62. I do what works.
